def test_SetupCfgCommandConfig():
    # Test basic construction with all required fields
    config = SetupCfgCommandConfig(
        name='build',
        camel='Build',
        description='Build the project',
        commands=('python setup.py build', 'python setup.py bdist_wheel')
    )
    assert config.name == 'build'
    assert config.camel == 'Build'
    assert config.description == 'Build the project'
    assert config.commands == ('python setup.py build', 'python setup.py bdist_wheel')

    # Test construction with empty values
    config = SetupCfgCommandConfig(
        name='',
        camel='',
        description='',
        commands=()
    )
    assert config.name == ''
    assert config.camel == ''
    assert config.description == ''
    assert config.commands == ()

    # Test that it behaves like a tuple
    config = SetupCfgCommandConfig(
        name='test',
        camel='Test',
        description='Run tests',
        commands=('pytest',)
    )
    assert isinstance(config, tuple)
    assert len(config) == 4
    assert config[0] == 'test'
    assert config[1] == 'Test'
    assert config[2] == 'Run tests'
    assert config[3] == ('pytest',)

    # Test unpacking
    name, camel, description, commands = config
    assert name == 'test'
    assert camel == 'Test'
    assert description == 'Run tests'
    assert commands == ('pytest',)

    # Test field access via _fields and _asdict
    assert SetupCfgCommandConfig._fields == ('name', 'camel', 'description', 'commands')
    assert config._asdict() == {
        'name': 'test',
        'camel': 'Test',
        'description': 'Run tests',
        'commands': ('pytest',)
    }

    # Test _replace
    replaced = config._replace(name='lint')
    assert replaced.name == 'lint'
    assert replaced.camel == 'Test'
    assert replaced is not config

    # Test equality
    config2 = SetupCfgCommandConfig(
        name='test',
        camel='Test',
        description='Run tests',
        commands=('pytest',)
    )
    assert config == config2

    # Test that missing arguments raise TypeError
    try:
        SetupCfgCommandConfig(name='build')  # type: ignore
        assert False, "Expected TypeError"
    except TypeError:
        pass

    import tempfile

        with open(os.path.join(setup_dir, 'setup.py'), 'w') as f:
            f.write('# setup.py\n')

                '[metadata]\n'
                'name = test_package\n'
                '\n'
                '[setup.command.build]\n'
                'description = Build the {name} package\n'
                'commands =\n'
                '    echo building {name}\n'
                '    echo setup_dir: {setup_dir}\n'
            )
        configs = list(each_sub_command_config(setup_dir))
        assert len(configs) == 1
        config = configs[0]
        assert isinstance(config, SetupCfgCommandConfig)
        assert config.name == 'build'
        assert config.camel == 'Build'
        assert config.description == 'Build the test_package package'
        assert config.commands == (
            'echo building test_package',
            'echo setup_dir: %s' % os.path.realpath(setup_dir),
        )

        # The 'name' option overrides the section-derived command name.
        with open(os.path.join(setup_dir, 'setup.cfg'), 'w') as f:
            f.write(
                '[metadata]\n'
                'name = test_package\n'
                '\n'
                '[setup.command.my-cmd]\n'
                'name = Custom Name\n'
                'commands = echo hi\n'
            )
        configs = list(each_sub_command_config(setup_dir))
        assert len(configs) == 1
        assert configs[0].name == 'Custom Name'
        assert configs[0].camel == 'CustomName'
        assert configs[0].description == ''
        assert configs[0].commands == ('echo hi',)

        # setup_commands.cfg, when present, replaces setup.cfg entirely.
        with open(os.path.join(setup_dir, 'setup_commands.cfg'), 'w') as f:
            f.write(
                '[setup.command.other]\n'
                'commands = echo other\n'
            )
        configs = list(each_sub_command_config(setup_dir))
        assert len(configs) == 1
        assert configs[0].name == 'other'
        assert configs[0].camel == 'Other'
        os.remove(os.path.join(setup_dir, 'setup_commands.cfg'))

        # Sections without commands, with empty command names, or with
        # non-identifier titles are skipped.
        with open(os.path.join(setup_dir, 'setup.cfg'), 'w') as f:
            f.write(
                '[metadata]\n'
                'name = test_package\n'
                '\n'
                '[setup.command.]\n'
                'commands = echo nope\n'
                '\n'
                '[setup.command.1bad]\n'
                'commands = echo nope\n'
                '\n'
                '[setup.command.empty]\n'
            )
        configs = list(each_sub_command_config(setup_dir))
        assert len(configs) == 0

        # A missing 'metadata' section raises LookupError.
        with open(os.path.join(setup_dir, 'setup.cfg'), 'w') as f:
            f.write('[setup.command.x]\ncommands = echo x\n')
        try:
            list(each_sub_command_config(setup_dir))
        except LookupError:
            pass
        else:
            raise AssertionError('LookupError was not raised')
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(setup_dir)
